findings.location: Lemma 9.1, PDF/printed p.36 last comparison chain
findings.claim: Upper Fubini product-domain kernel is comparable to |x-y|^-2.
findings.assumptions_checked: Unit circle is smooth closed chord-arc; d in (0,pi/8); s=pi; printed arcs are two semicircles.
findings.verification: Printed kernel J(d)=pi integral_d^(pi+d)(2sin(w/2))^-4 dw ~ pi/(3d^3). With |z-w| denominator the enlarged arcs overlap and diagonal integral is infinite.
findings.counterevidence: Circle has finite Mobius and tangent energies; theorem not refuted.
findings.impact: Invalid core derivation of Definitions 7 iff 8 / Theorem 1.2.
findings.repair: Retain a+b+d<=length/2; chord-arc gives kernel upper <=2C^4/(6d^2), lower from a,b in [0,d]; large separated pairs bounded.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: The actual Lemma9.1 upper Fubini comparison enlarges the shorter-arc incidence domain to two full length-half-circumference arcs, while asserting a d^-2 kernel.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: The smooth chord-arc unit circle satisfies every assumption. For x0,yd with0<d<pi/8, the printed product kernel is pi*integral_d^(d+pi)(2sin(w/2))^-4 dw ~pi/(3d^3), not d^-2. Multiplication by the tangent-difference square~d^2 then produces a divergent intermediate integral. Replacing only the denominator by |z-w|^-4 makes the overlapping-arc diagonal integral infinite.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Retaining a,b>=0 and a+b+d<=length/2 gives upper C^4/(3d^2), using the exact quadrant integral1/(6d^2). For d<=length/8, a,b in[0,d] gives a lower1/(81d^2). Large separated pairs contribute a finite bounded amount. This repairs the finite-energy equivalence; it does not assert a uniform pointwise lower comparison at the half-length endpoint.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: An invalid central proof estimate in Definitions7/8 and Theorem1.2, hence Major under the specified standard, even though the corrected argument supports the theorem.

findings.claim: Normal-boundary-sphere center displacement O(t sup|kappa|), and rho(Q)=O(K_r).
findings.assumptions_checked: Round circle, properly embedded complete totally geodesic hemisphere, n=2 allowed, curvature zero and square integral zero.
findings.verification: At x^2+t^2=1, normal geodesic center 1/x differs from x by t^2/x>0. Endpoints (1+-t)/x multiply to 1. Antipodal reflection R(z)=1/conjugate(z) has Euclidean derivative norm |z|^-2 !=1 off circle while K_r=0.
findings.counterevidence: rho(Q)=O(diam Q) for inversion near circle, so the square sum is finite; existence conclusion survives.
findings.impact: Quantitative core implication (16)->(13) not established by printed estimate.
findings.repair: Requires Euclidean scale term, foliation justification and an L2 local-supremum estimate; no general replacement proved.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Definition13 uses Euclidean local distance distortion, and Lemma18.2 bounds the normal-boundary-sphere center displacement and reflection distortion solely by hyperbolic principal curvatures.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: The complete properly embedded totally geodesic unit hemisphere is permitted with all principal curvatures0 and curvature square integral0. At x^2+t^2=1 the normal geodesic center is1/x, displaced by t^2/x>0, and its boundary endpoints(1+-t)/x have product1. The induced antipodal reflection is1/conjugate(z), whose Euclidean derivative norm|z|^-2 differs from1 off the circle even though K_r=0.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Hyperbolic normalization does not remove the Euclidean scale term. In this round case rho(Q)=O(diamQ) and the square sum converges, so the existential reflection conclusion survives. A general replacement needs background-scale, normal-foliation and L2 local-supremum controls; the generic bump diagnostic is not falsely presented as an actual minimal-surface counterexample.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for the false quantitative core(16)->(13) derivation, without claiming the existential equivalence is false or a complete repair is proved.

findings.assumptions_checked: Round WP circle, delta=0, totally geodesic minimal disk, chi=1, every height 0<t<1 regular.
findings.verification: kappa_g=1/sqrt(1-t^2); L=2pi sqrt(1-t^2)/t; A=2pi(1/t-1); trace=2pi(1-sqrt(1-t^2))/t>0 while asserted bound is zero.
findings.counterevidence: Trace tends to zero and RA=-2pi, consistent with final formula.
findings.impact: Invalid boundary estimate in core (15)->(19) and renormalized-area derivation.
findings.repair: Must retain scale/background error, prove integrated trace control, and replace the nonescaping S_t minus S_(t+1) annulus; general proof pending.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Lemma20.1 applies to height truncations and asserts a boundary error controlled by delta^2. The original p49 definition gives delta0 for the round circle.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: The round WP boundary and totally geodesic minimal disk have delta=kappa0,chi1, and every0<t<1 is a regular height. With r=sqrt(1-t^2), L=2pi r/t, A=2pi(1/t-1),kappa_g=1/r; hence integral(kappa_g-1)dL=2pi(1-r)/t>0 while the claimed delta^2 bound is0.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The boundary term tends0 and the actual renormalized area equals-2pi, so the final formula is not disproved. An O(t^2) pointwise background term integrates toO(t) in the round case only. The printed S_t minus S_(t+1) annulus does not escape compact subsets; an S_t minus S_(2t) annulus would, but its required general trace comparison still needs proof.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for the invalid core renormalized-area boundary estimate, with general repair and all-minimal-surface scope explicitly unresolved.

findings.claim: rho comparable to sqrt(epsilon/r) for all disjoint equal-radius balls.
findings.assumptions_checked: Radius r>0, positive gap epsilon, arbitrary eta=epsilon/r satisfies printed assumptions.
findings.verification: rho=2acosh(1+eta/2); rho/sqrt(eta)->2 at zero and ->0 at infinity.
findings.counterevidence: Lemma 16.3 uses small epsilon_Gamma<1/100, so its application avoids large eta.
findings.repair: Assume bounded small eta or state exact formula.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Lemma16.1 imposes disjoint equal-radius balls, without a small gap-to-radius condition.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: For eta=epsilon/r>0, rho=2acosh(1+eta/2). rho/sqrt(eta) tends2 near0 but0 aseta grows, excluding the claimed uniform two-sided comparison on its full stated range.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: A fixed bounded small eta range gives the comparison, or use the exact formula. The next relevant application imposes epsilon_Gamma<1/100.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for an auxiliary range overstatement; the actual small-gap core use is not refuted.

findings.claim: Smooth curves have finite E^(j,p) when jp<=2p+1.
findings.assumptions_checked: Smooth embedded unit circle, j=3,p=1, equality 3=2+1.
findings.counterevidence: Main Mobius case j=2,p=1 lies strictly inside threshold.
findings.repair: For j,p>0 use jp<2p+1; at nonzero curvature equality diverges.

independent_verification.source_claim_check: Section23 includes equality jp=2p+1 in its smooth-curve finiteness claim.
independent_verification.hypotheses_and_decisive_check: The smooth embedded unit circle withj3,p1 is admissible. (2sin(h/2))^-3-h^-3=1/(8h)+17h/1920+O(h^3), giving positive logarithmic divergence at the diagonal. This is an analytic local singularity test, not a conclusion from numerical integration.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: At nonzero curvature the local integrand is of order |h|^(p(2-j)), so j,p>0 require the strict inequality jp<2p+1. Main Mobius casej2,p1 lies strictly inside.
independent_verification.dependency_and_severity: Retain Minor for the peripheral endpoint, with no added adverse conclusion about Theorem1.2.

scope_clarifications.location: Definition 20 p.28; Lemma 12.1 pp.40-41; Lemma 22.1 p.60
scope_clarifications.result: Single vertex-based square cylinder has finite RA but square not WP; aligned weighted sum 8-4sqrt2, shifted basepoint 1/3 has constant positive weighted deficit.
scope_clarifications.counterevidence: Theorem 1.3 and Lemma 12.1 explicitly require all basepoints uniformly; Definition20 can import this through its reference. Not counted as a counterexample to these statements.

scope_clarifications.result: Smooth quasisymmetric welding t^3 maps by conformal power maps to a half-disk boundary with two corners; homeomorphism regularity alone insufficient.
scope_clarifications.counterevidence: Next paragraph specifies diffeomorphisms; an implicit WP restriction also excludes the example.
scope_clarifications.required_reading: Specify nondegenerate H^s diffeomorphism or the intended WP domain; no theorem counterexample under these stronger assumptions.

scope_clarifications.result: Fat-ball incidence and gap normalization must be retained; otherwise remote huge balls make the infimum trivial.
scope_clarifications.counterevidence: Figure and later use supply intended local geometry; treated as restoration of definition, not separate issue.

independent_scope_check.conclusion: Retain three Major and two Minor findings. The corrected short-arc Fubini argument is locally verified; the two hyperbolic-to-Euclidean/height-trace repairs remain limited and do not become theorem counterexamples. Existing scope clarifications and two Needs Evidence items remain outside proved-defect counts. No scientific TeX/PDF change is required.
counterevidence_and_limits: Only the author-hosted black-and-white proof PDF created2025-06-17 is bound; publisher Version of Record equivalence is not established.
Neither general reflection repair nor general boundary trace/all-minimal-surface argument is certified. NE1 and NE2 remain open.
Single-basepoint square and degenerate smooth-welding tests are retained as scope clarifications because the main theorem's stronger quantifiers/diffeomorphism conditions exclude them.

The auxiliary's source passages and five actual source-page images, and root report lines76-312, are the new focused reading. Original78-page whole-paper coverage and eleven report-page inspections are reused historical evidence, not new full reads.
